subject: CALL-CONVENTION directive
notes: Rule: "The default for the CALL-CONVENTION directive is '>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL'." (cite.py: OK §7.3.9.3 1)). The compiler holds no call-convention state (DirectiveStateRegistry row: 'every name is processed under the §7.3.9.3 GR1 default (COBOL)'), so with no directive every CALL/CANCEL/program-address/INVOKE name is processed under the COBOL mapping. Probe probe/callconv/A.cob (no directive): CALL "ccsubA" and CALL "CCSUBA" both reach PROGRAM-ID CCSUBA -> 'IN SUB' twice at 2023; same at --std 2002 (B.cob). The explicit '>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL' (B.cob) is indistinguishable, as GR1 requires. --std 85 rejects the directive with COBOL0900 (facility introduced 2002). No spec-derived test asserts the default mapping (tests/conformance/2002/pb725_directive_facility.cob only proves the directive compiles and says 'no call convention varies here'), so test-ref empty. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility; absent in COBOL-85)
